 reported third-quarter results with double-digit revenue growth, led by its immunology medicines Skyrizi and Rinvoq. The biopharmaceutical company raised its full-year earnings outlook again and announced another increase to its quarterly dividend, beginning early next year. For readers who follow Dividend Stocks, AbbVie is one of the most widely followed income names in healthcare, with a long record of annual dividend increases. It is a major pharmaceutical company on the NYSE Composite. Net revenue increased at a double-digit pace compared with a year earlier. Both GAAP and adjusted earnings per share more than doubled, helped by much lower charges for acquired research and development compared with the prior year. Adjusted operating margin was strong, reflecting the high profitability of AbbVie's leading medicines. AbbVie's board approved a mid-single-digit increase to the quarterly dividend, beginning with the payment in February next year. The company is a member of the S&P Dividend Aristocrats Index, which tracks companies that have raised their dividends for many consecutive years. Since becoming an independent company, AbbVie has grown its dividend substantially, and its history of increases extends back to its time as part of Abbott Laboratories. Skyrizi and Rinvoq are AbbVie's largest growth drivers. Both medicines treat immune-related conditions such as psoriasis, arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease. Each grew at a strong double-digit pace during the quarter. Humira was once the world's top revenue-generating medicine, but its sales have declined sharply since lower-cost biosimilar versions entered the market. Skyrizi and Rinvoq have more than made up for that loss, allowing AbbVie to return to strong growth. AbbVie recently presented new data showing disease control for patients with inflammatory bowel disease. Skyrizi also gained an additional approval option for Crohn's disease, and a combination therapy showed encouraging early results. The neuroscience portfolio grew strongly, led by Vraylar, Botox Therapeutic for migraines and other conditions, and the migraine treatment Ubrelvy. Oncology revenue was broadly flat, while the aesthetics portfolio, which includes Botox Cosmetic and Juvederm, declined slightly as consumer spending on cosmetic procedures stayed soft. AbbVie raised its full-year adjusted earnings per share guidance range. The updated outlook includes the impact of acquired research and development costs recorded so far this year. Management pointed to strong momentum across its diverse portfolio. AbbVie combines a sizable dividend with steady growth from new medicines. Its strong cash flow supports both dividend increases and investments in research and acquisitions. For investors seeking reliable income from healthcare, this balance of yield and growth is a key attraction. AbbVie continues to invest in new treatments across immunology, neuroscience and oncology, both through internal research and acquisitions. Its pipeline aims to extend growth well beyond its current blockbusters. Recent late-stage data and regulatory submissions support future product launches. AbbVie's leading medicines carry very high margins, generating strong operating cash flow. This cash funds the dividend, debt repayment and investments in research and acquisitions. A high adjusted gross margin during the quarter shows the profitability of its portfolio, which supports the company's ability to keep raising its payout. AbbVie's aesthetics business, which includes Botox Cosmetic and dermal fillers, has faced softer demand as consumers cut back on discretionary spending. This segment is sensitive to economic conditions, so a recovery in consumer confidence would help. Management continues to invest in marketing and new products to support long-term growth here. Risks include competition for Skyrizi and Rinvoq, US drug pricing reforms, weakness in aesthetics, clinical trial outcomes and debt from past acquisitions. Interest expense remains meaningful because of borrowing tied to earlier deals. AbbVie's dividend growth has been faster than many large pharmaceutical peers. Its successful transition away from Humira sets it apart from companies still facing major patent expirations. This has allowed AbbVie to keep raising its dividend while investing in future growth. Neuroscience has become one of AbbVie's fastest-growing areas, covering conditions such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, migraine and Parkinson's disease. Strong demand for Vraylar and migraine treatments shows the value of this portfolio. Adding new neuroscience medicines helps diversify AbbVie's revenue beyond immunology. Key indicators include Skyrizi and Rinvoq growth, neuroscience momentum, aesthetics recovery, pipeline updates and next year's guidance. AbbVie's third quarter showed strong growth from its immunology leaders, a raised earnings outlook and another dividend increase. Its successful shift beyond Humira and growing neuroscience portfolio support its appeal as a dividend-focused healthcare company, while competition and pricing reforms remain areas to watch. AbbVie Inc., a research-based biopharmaceutical company, engages in the research and development, manufacturing, commercializing, and sale of medicines and therapies worldwide. The company offers Skyrizi to treat autoimmune diseases; Rinvoq to treat inflammatory diseases; Imbruvica for the treatment of adult patients with blood cancers; Venclexta to treat blood cancers; Elahere to treat various cancer; and Epkinly to treat lymphoma; and Emrelis for the treatment of lung cancer. It also provides facial injectables, plastics and regenerative medicine, body contouring, and skincare products; botox Cosmetic for the treatment of glabellar lines, crow's feet, forehead lines, and platysma bands; Juvederm Collection to treat volume loss in the temples, undereye, cheeks, chin, lips and lower face; Vraylar to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and depressive disorder; Duodopa to treat Parkinson's disease; Ubrelvy to treat migraine; Qulipta for episodic and chronic migraine; and Vyalev for the treatment of motor fluctuations, as well as Botox Therapeutic to treat chronic migraine, overactive bladder, spasticity, cervical dystonia, and other conditions. In addition, the company offers Ozurdex for visual impairment; Lumigan/Ganfort and Alphagan/Combigan for the reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension; and other eye care products, including Refresh/Optive, Xen, Durysta, and Restasis. Further, it provides Mavyret to treat chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 1-6 infection; Creon, a pancreatic enzyme therapy; and Linzess/Constella to treat irritable bowel syndrome with constipation and chronic idiopathic constipation.
